sentences.text: The teeth of Protosqualus feature an undulated ventral margin on the dental crown located distal to the apron, unlike modern Squalus sharks which show high labiolingual compression. The holotype of P. sigei possesses teeth with small gaps between them, each ending in a clearly defined slanted tip.

Protosqualus argentinensis is believed to have been the largest member of the genus, characterized by defined serrated cutting edges on its teeth. Some Protosqualus species, including P. barringtonensis, exhibit high levels of heterodonty, meaning their teeth vary significantly in shape.

The type species Protosqualus sigei was discovered in an Albian-aged rock deposit in France. The name Protosqualus translates to "primitive Squalus" because it is an ancient relative of the modern genus Squalus.

Fossils of Protosqualus teeth are frequently found in the Grey Chalk deposit in England. Protosqualus went extinct at the end of the Cretaceous period, with the last known species, P. argentinensis, found in southern Argentina and possibly earlier deposits in India.
Protosqualus shared Cretaceous oceans with other chondrichthyans, fish, and marine reptiles like mosasaurs and plesiosaurs.
Protosqualus is classified as a member of the family Squalidae within the order Squaliformes. A 2001 study by Adnet and Cappetta identified Protosqualus as the sister taxon to the genus Squalus.

Protosqualus lived between the Barremian and Campanian stages, approximately 125.77 to 72.2 million years ago. The Calafate Formation, where Protosqualus fossils have been found, likely consisted of estuaries and shallow seas.
